item.title: Jeff Garcia calls for coaching change at alma mater San Jose State, nominates himself
item.description: Football: Legends of Candlestick: Former San Francisco 49ers QB Jeff Garcia in action, making pass during flag football game at Candlestick Park. San Francisco, CA 7/12/2014. (Brad Mangin/Sports Illustrated via Getty Ima) Former San Jose State quarterback Jeff Garcia has nominated himself to take over and revive his alma mater's struggling football program. In a sudden Instagram post Monday, Garcia shared a photo of himself when he played for the Spartans from 1991 to 1993, along with a long caption bemoaning the direction of the team. "We sit here as Former Spartans constantly waiting for that certain someone to bring us that competitive mindset to achieve greatness on and off the field," the post reads. "We bring outsiders in, but never look at those who wore and bled for the blue and gold as our potential leader. Why not? What do we have to lose?" View this post on Instagram A post shared by Jeff Garcia (@jeffgarciaqb5) Thus, the pitch for himself began. Gracia noted that since 1996, the Spartans have only had seven winning seasons, seven bowl appearances (with a 3-4 record) and two Top 25 appearances. Garcia continued, "Now if that's a record worth standing behind… then continue to go through life blinded by reality." Garcia argues that if Indiana was able to become a national powerhouse by bringing in two- and three-star recruits in the landscape of paid players, then San Jose State can do that too, albeit on a smaller scale by winning the conference. He wants the team to rebuild in the image of the Hoosiers and bring in "a great leader who players believe in and a coaching staff who is motivated and driven to bringing the best out of these young men and to put them in a scheme that gives them the confidence and mentality to compete with anyone and everyone." That person: him. "The ultimate goal is to win the league against teams who are your equal," Garcia's post concludes. "There's no reason why we can't get there and I'm here to help the Spartans redefine their mentality and bring a program back to life. A program that expects to win and will fight, scratch, and claw every time they step on to that field! WHO's WITH ME?" Garcia doesn't outright say what job he is asking for, other than saying "I'm here to help the Spartans" after earlier referencing the team's need for a "leader," but his post reads like a pitch for a coaching role rather than a general manager role, like Cal has with Ron Rivera or Stanford has with Andrew Luck . Indiana, who is Garcia's city upon a hill in his post, does not have a GM role, but a lot has been made of how head coach Curt Cignetti changed the culture of the program. Garcia, who played for the 49ers from 1999 to 2003, has had two coaching stints in his career. One as a quarterbacks coach for the CFL's Montreal Alouettes in 2014, and served as an offensive assistant for the St. Louis Rams in 2015. San Jose State football could use some help. item.title: Victor Wembanyama talks limits of 'villain' label, going barefoot and more
item.description: Spurs player Victor Wembanyama spoke on going barefoot, meditating, how chess impacts his game and much more on CBS 60 Minutes on November 1, 2026. (Photo by Alex Goodlett/Getty Images) (Alex Goodlett/Getty Images) Victor Wembanyama is already known for a few things off the basketball court: reading , committing to the perfect Halloween costume, meditating with monks in China. But in a new spotlight on CBS 60 Minutes , the Spurs forward-center pulled back the curtain even more. Sitting down with journalist Jon Wertheim on the November 1 episode of the program, Wemby got personal, including how his blood clot diagnosis made him want to be less guarded - because life is so short, "I don't even wanna waste it being somebody else." He went on to talk about the similarities between chess and basketball, the difference between social interactions in France and America, being mentored by Gregg Popovich and how it felt to host his fellow Spurs back home in Paris this summer. He also dove into why he loves to go barefoot. The episode said the 7-foot-4-inch, so-called alien is "obsessed" with his feet and sees them as the key to his career. According to him, "big men have always had feet problems," making him a big proponent of finding the right shoe (or ditching them altogether). It's so important to him because shoes that "respect the natural shape of the foot" help build foot strength, which in turn improves posture, knee, hip and back health. "It's funny, because I was just talking to a rookie. I went to practice barefoot, and he sees me walking without shoes, and he's like, 'I didn't know you could just not wear shoes,'" Wembanyama said. He added that he tries to walk around barefoot as much as possible or with minimalist shoes that don't have a thick sole. By the way, he wears a size 20, according to CBS. Victor Wembanyama says playoff fouls showed his limits The interview also touched on some notable moments from the 2026 playoffs. Who could forget the elbow laid into then-Minnesota Timberwolves center Naz Reid, and later appearing to drop the Knicks' Jalen Brunson to the floor? Wertheim asked Wembanyama if that showed the league a different side of him, an "edgy Wemby." But the Spur had a different take, though he also said he doesn't think any player in the Finals pays attention to those "villain" labels. "It showed my limits more than anything else," he said. "Going out there, you need to play basketball. You don't need to beat the sh*t out of people. If you wanna win, at least." But lastly, there's one thing to know about Wemby, and you might have picked up on it already from his affinity for fantasy novels, learning from different mentors and more. He said his curiosity is "the defining trait of mine." The Spurs play at home on Monday, November 2, against the Utah Jazz. item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon State’s loss at Fresno State
item.description: FRESNO, Calif. — Oregon State lost to Fresno State 38-22 Saturday night at Valley Children’s Stadium. Here are 10 takeaways as the Beavers prepare to host Texas State. 1. Reality check Two things can be true. Oregon State can still be ahead of schedule and on its way to a legitimately surprising season amid a massive rebuild, complete with a potent offense. Much of its success thus far came by pounding less talented teams and several of the worst defenses in the country. And where OSU was vulnerable was there to be exploited by teams like Fresno State, which has talent and good coaching. The Beavers are not a College Football Playoff team. That dose of reality doesn’t diminish what’s being accomplished this season. They’re simply not one of the two most talented teams in the Pac-12 right now. 2. Oregon State was outcoached JaMarcus Shephard and his staff were outcoached for definitely the first time in conference play and arguably for the first time this season. Matt Entz laid out in detail what Fresno State picked up from studying Braden Atkinson from his time at Mercer and Oregon State’s tendencies. Bye weeks also include self-scouting. Fresno State was more prepared for what OSU showed and particularly offensively the Beavers did not have an effective counter. 3. Self-inflicted errors can’t happen in games like this Winning on the road against a team with at least comparable (if not better) talent and coaching is a difficult task to begin with. It becomes a whole lot harder with six presnap penalties and allowing five sacks with two leading to fumbles. OSU absolutely could have led by multiple scores early if not for a false start negating Jake Reichle’s would-be touchdown, if Aeryn Hampton’s foot was in bounds and if multiple other penalties didn’t occur. That doesn’t even get into defensive miscues from missed tackles or over-pursuits. 4. The offensive line may have had its worst game Houston was more physically dominating than Fresno State, but that’s to be expected. Oregon State’s offensive line had a brutal showing nearly across the board, with sacks allowed by multiple players in one-on-one matchups. OSU’s rushing stats are skewed by the sacks and not nearly as poor as the final box score, but the bottom line is Fresno State won the line of scrimmage and it’s not a particularly stout group. 5. Josiah Freeman was the best receiver on the field Fresno State’s 6-foot-4 receiver had a big night with two touchdowns. Freeman had a massive advantage against Isaiah Houi and performed accordingly. If there’s one piece OSU’s receiving corps is missing it is a target with the size and length of Freeman, which the Beavers are leaning on via their tight ends. But an outside target like him is hard to beat and he showed why. 6. item.description: Nov 2, 2026; Syracuse, New York, USA; Syracuse Orange head coach Gerry McNamara reacts during the first half against the New Haven Chargers at the JMA Wireless Dome. Just days after his father’s passing, McNamara coached Syracuse to a 74-58 win from the JMA Wireless Dome in the season-opener. Syracuse held New Haven to just 25.9% first half shooting and led by as many as 28 on the game but let off the gas in the second half to hold on to a 15-point victory. Gavin Doty and Sadiq White led the way for Syracuse, each posting a double-double. Doty had 14 points and 13 rebounds while White had 14 point and 10 rebounds. Sixth-man Kiyan Anthony led Syracuse in scoring with 17 points. Orange guard Aiden Tobiason was out as he continues to work through a hamstring issue. Syracuse went with a starting five of Garwey Dual, Doty, Mark Morano, White and Luke Wilson. Doty got things started for Syracuse with a three following an offensive rebound by White. Doty scored the Orange’s first five points and Morano hit back-to-back threes as Syracuse led 12-0 at the first media timeout. Kiyan Anthony checked in first off the bench after the first stoppage in play. Ryan Moesch, Amarri Monroe and Abdramane Siby rounded out the nine-man rotation. Anthony scored four quick points off the bench following a mid-range jumpshot and two free throws as the Orange extended its lead 18-0. New Haven started 0-11 from the floor before making its first shot – a Moussa Camara floater over the outstretched 7-foot-6 wingspan of Siby. Without much resistance in its man defense, New Haven went 2-3 zone despite Orange sharpshooter Morano in the game. Anthony connected a corner three against the zone for nine first half points. The Orange had a chance to extend the lead after a pair of defensive stands but an errant Moesch pass on the break and an out of control that ended in an Anthony missed three, McNamara reinserted Dual into the game. item.title: Atlético Madrid’s Álex Baena counting on home strength vs. Bayern Munich
item.description: (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) | Getty Images Atlético Madrid midfielder Álex Baena knows his team faces one of its biggest tests of the Champions League campaign when Bayern Munich visit the Metropolitano tomorrow. The Spaniard recognizes the quality Vincent Kompany’s side possesses but believes Atlético’s ho me advantage could prove important against one of Europe’s elite clubs. Baena also sees the matchup as an opportunity for his team to measure itself against some of the best players in the world. “Bayern are one of the best teams in the world, with some outstanding players, and I think this is a very exciting challenge for us, a chance to see how far we can go in this Champions League campaign. But I think we’re fortunate to be playing at home, in front of our own fans. Ultimately, every opponent finds it difficult to get points here. We’re very strong at home, and I think tomorrow’s game is one that every player wants to be involved in, given the quality of the opposition and the players they have,” said Baena (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). There is little doubt that Atlético will be looking to make the most of their home surroundings. The Metropolitano can be an intimidating venue, and Diego Simeone’s t eams have built much of their identity around making life miserable for visiting opponents. However, Baye rn will not be traveling to Madrid simply to admire the atmosphere or the opposition’s talent. Despite their injury problems, the Bavarians have more than enough quality to make this a very uncomfortable evening for Atlético, too. item.description: HOLLAND TWP. - As the West Ottawa volleyball team faced another set point and looked to be headed to a fifth set, Ellie Hulst took over. Down 24-23, Hulst slammed a kill down the line. She had two more in the next few points and the Panthers hung on to beat Zeeland West 25-23, 25-12, 18-25, 27-25 in the first round of the Division 1 district tournament on Monday, Nov. 2, at West Ottawa. "She is definitely an anchor for our offense," West Ottawa coach Kaitlyn Lawton said. "She is a cool, calm and collected player. She never gets too high or too low and thrives in competition. She always seems to get it done and find the spaces. It is easy to lean on her when we need to." item.title: High school boys soccer: Washington nets Super-Sectional win, spot in IHSA 2A semis
item.description: URBANA — Washington’s high school boys soccer team took a big step in its path toward an IHSA Class 2A championship on Monday with a victory in the Urbana Super-Sectional . Panthers senior defender Truman Lenover notched the only goal of the match, delivering the game-winner just 4:39 after the opening kickoff to defeat Troy Triad, 1-0 at Urbana High School. Washington advanced to the IHSA Class 2A state semifinals, where it will face the winner of the Grayslake Central Super-Sectional between Vernon Hills-Crystal Lake South. That state semifinal match is 2:30 p.m. Friday at Rockford Guilford. Lenover set up among a pack of defenders in front of the Triad goal, and leaped to head in a high, arching throw-in from the right sideline with 35:21 still to go in the first half. Sophomore goalkeeper Oliver Wettstein tossed the team’s 21 st shutout of the season and Washington improved to 22-1-2 while Troy’s season ended at 19-4-3. The Panthers had 22 shutouts last season, tied for second-most in a single season in state history, and one short of the IHSA record. item.title: Kentucky WBB flashes freshman brilliance and vet dominance in opening win vs. Morehead State
item.description: Kentucky Wildcats women’s basketball is officially back. The Cats hit the floor Monday against the Morehead Eagles and wasted very little time getting the offense rolling. By halftime, Kentucky had built a commanding 42-15 lead, showcasing a perfect blend of veterans and freshman potential. The first half’s story was undoubtedly the immediate impact of the highly touted freshman class. All three first-year players scored and impacted the game in other ways, too. At halftime, head coach Kenny Brooks said he would need to adjust his rotations because he has so many capable players. Remember, Kenny relies heavily on 6 players, even going back to his Va Tech days. I don’t think he can do that here. Savvy Swords was the very first player off the bench, and she immediately made an impression by draining her first shot of the game. By the break, she was already flirting with a double-double, racking up six points and six rebounds in just nine minutes. Meanwhile, Maddyn Greenway proved that her game is about much more than just putting the ball in the hoop. While she arrived in Lexington as the third-highest scoring high school women’s player of all time, her defensive intensity stole the show in the first two quarters. Greenway was locked into her stance, applying relentless pressure, and even sacrificed her body to take a hard charge. She and fellow freshman Emily McDonald each chipped in a basket, ensuring the entire freshman trio got on the board in their debut half. Greenway finished with 12 points, 3 rebounds, and 4 assists. Saavy Swords had 6 points and 11 rebounds, while Emily McDonald added 10 points. Down in the paint, the veterans anchored the blowout. Clara Strack was every bit as dominant as expected. The senior center bullied her way to a game-high 17 points; she added 9 rebounds, 6 blocks, and 3 assists. Ajša Sivka was also huge, adding 12 points and 8 assists as a 6’5 wing. Few teams can have a player who can do that at her height. Me’Arah O’Neal had 10 points and 7 rebounds. The only slight hiccup for the Wildcats came from the perimeter, where Asia Boone couldn’t get going offensively. She started cold and never warmed up, making just 1-of-7 field goals and 0-of-5 from deep. The Cats will have no complaints, though; they won 85-43. Up next is Thursday night against Northern Kentucky at 6:30.

item.description: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images The man who once sat on the bench for the Kansas City Chiefs is now the starter for the team coming to town to play them. Josh Weinfuss of ESPN reported that Gardner Minshew, formerly with the Chiefs, has become the starting quarterback for the Arizona Cardinals. Consequently, he faces his old team when Arizona visits Arrowhead on November 22nd. It is a twist no one saw coming for a player who was just a backup a year ago. During the 2025 offseason, Minshew agreed to a one-year, $1.17 million deal with the Chiefs to serve as Patrick Mahomes’ backup. The experience in Kansas City became painful for him when Mahomes sustained a season-ending ACL and LCL injury during Week 15. Although Minshew started against the Tennessee Titans in Week 16, he broke his tibial plateau during that contest, ending his season. Signing with the Cardinals in the 2026 offseason, he replaced starter Jacoby Brissett last week. He guided the squad to a 33-30 win over the Dallas Cowboys. A Team Reeling From a Collapse The Chiefs need this win badly after a terrible loss to the Denver Broncos on Sunday, November 1. Overturning an 11-point hole, the Broncos scored 15 straight points in the fourth quarter to stun the Chiefs 28-24 and claim the division lead. Following a 5-0 start, the Chiefs have dropped consecutive games, including a lopsided loss last weekend to Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. Sky Sports NFL’s Jeff Reinebold said on Inside the Huddle, “It will be one that is gonna haunt them for a long time because this was a game where they could have taken control of the division.” Patrick Mahomes walked off the field with a series of facial expressions that showed disappointment, frustration and regret. Leading by 11 points late in the second half, the Chiefs surrendered the lead and their AFC West standing to the Broncos due to a mistake-ridden fourth quarter. “The execution just wasn’t at a high enough level,” Mahomes said. “We made big plays, and we made plays happen against a really good defense, but you’ve got to execute for the full 60 minutes. We weren’t able to do it.” Can Simmons Return for the Fight? Minshew returning to Kansas City might not be the primary narrative of that matchup. Josh Simmons, an offensive tackle, will become eligible for activation off injured reserve for the first time this week. He will have sat out the mandatory four games before facing Arizona. Since injuring his back with a bulging disc during training camp, Simmons has not played this season. He resumed practice in Week 6 but did not see action against the Los Angeles Chargers. A setback occurred the next week, leading to the choice to put Simmons on IR. Simmons returning against the Cardinals would be excellent news. While rookie Kahlil Benson has done well under pressure, Simmons represents a significant improvement. The Chiefs face a three-game stretch where taking care of business will be crucial. item.title: Bo Van Pelt Locks In 2026 WITB For Fall Season
item.description: Bo Van Pelt hits out of bunker on hole No. 18 during the Kaulig Companies PGA Championship Final Round, July 12, 2026, at Firestone Country Club in Akron, Ohio. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Bo Van Pelt has finalized his equipment setup for the October 2026 tournament season, showing a blend of Callaway, Srixon, and Cleveland gear. The veteran player made these specific choices public on November 1, just as the fall swing kicked into high gear. GolfWRX broke the story with detailed in-hand photos that confirm every shaft and head in the bag. This lineup highlights a preference for specific steel shafts and modern driver technology designed for the PGA Tour’s latest course setups. The driver situation sees Van Pelt relying on the Callaway Quantum Max set at 9 degrees. He pairs this with a Fujikura Ventus Black 6 X shaft to generate stability off the tee. For shorter tee shots, the bag holds a Cobra King TEC-MD mini driver at 13 degrees, fitted with a Fujikura Ventus Blue 7 X shaft. Fairway wood duties fall to a Ping G440 Max at 21 degrees, which uses a heavier Fujikura Ventus Black 8 X shaft for added control. GolfWRX noted these specific loft and shaft combinations are critical for his trajectory on longer holes. Van Pelt’s iron and utility setup leans heavily on Srixon models. He carries Srixon ZXi5 irons in the 5-iron slot and Srixon ZXi7 models for the 6-iron through pitching wedge range. Both iron sets utilize Nippon N.S. Pro Modus3 Tour125 S shafts. The utility section features a Srixon ZXiU at 20 degrees with a Fujikura Ventus HB Blue 8 X shaft, alongside a Srixon ZX at 23 degrees fitted with a Nippon N.S. Pro Modus3 Tour125 S shaft. This mix allows him to hit specific distances while maintaining a consistent feel through the bag. Short game equipment includes Cleveland RTZ 2 wedges in 50 and 60 degrees. The 50-degree wedge has a mid-sole grind, while the 58 and 60-degree models feature the 588-8 grind. These wedges are fitted with Nippon N.S. Pro WV125 Tour Only shafts. Van Pelt putts with an Odyssey Ai-One CH #7. He grips his clubs with Golf Pride MCC+4 Midsize and Golf Pride Victory Cord options depending on the shot. The ball of choice remains the Titleist Pro V1, a staple for Tour professionals seeking consistency. Why The Shaft Choices Matter He uses Nippon steel shafts for his irons and wedges, which suggests a preference for a specific kick point and feel. The driver and fairway woods switch to Fujikura Ventus models, known for their stability and low spin characteristics. GolfWRX reported that these specific shafts help him manage the ball flight when wind is a factor during fall events. Van Pelt decided to keep his Callaway driver and Ping fairway wood. The mini driver from Cobra adds versatility for tight tee boxes. The setup lets him hit a high percentage of fairways while still having the distance to reach par‑5s in two shots. This equipment list gives fans a clear look at what Van Pelt will use in upcoming tournaments.

item.title: LaVell’s innovation changed football forever
item.description: 20001118 BYU football coach LaVell Edwards watches his team as the sun sets in his eyes during his final game at Cougar (now LaVell Edwards Stadium) on Saturday, Nov. 18, 2000. | CHUCK WING Editor’s note: Seventh in an occasional series exploring LaVell Edwards’ legacy of leadership. In 1971, the average home price in America was $25,200, the hourly minimum wage was $1.60, a group of guys in Los Angeles formed a band called the Eagles , and LaVell Edwards was summoned to sit down with BYU President Dallin H. Oaks. The only thing that stayed the same after that was the band. Everything else went up, including Edwards’ coaching career. “(President) Oaks just called my dad into the room, just the two of them, and said, ‘They tell me you’re a pretty good coach and that you are easy to work with. So, do you want to be our head coach?’” recounted John Edwards, LaVell’s oldest son. “My dad said, ‘Well, yeah.’ They sat there for a minute, and President Oaks says, ‘Well, don’t you think we ought to tell somebody I just hired you? There is the sports information office in the athletic department, go call them and tell them you just got hired.’ So, my dad literally had to tell the people in the office that he got hired as head coach.” Fast-forward 29 years to another special visit — this time with President Gordon B. Hinckley of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. Edwards’ Cougars had just defeated New Mexico in his final home game as head coach. Surrounded by his wife Patti and his family, the soon-to-be Hall of Famer stood at midfield and watched as President Hinckley announced that Cougar Stadium was being renamed in his honor: LaVell Edwards Stadium. Patti and LaVell Edwards with President Gordon B. Hinckley on Nov. 18, 2000. | Mark Philbrick, BYU The shortest distance between two points is a straight line. For Edwards, the distance between his unceremonious hiring and his unprecedented retiring as the winningest coach in BYU history was a straight pass, or at least one that moved the ball upfield like no one had ever seen before. Pioneering the forward pass “Who knew that he was the pioneer, right? He’s a pioneer in the forward pass,” said former BYU Hall of Fame quarterback Steve Young (1980-83). “That wasn’t the first time anyone threw the ball, but it was the first time in college that people committed completely to it. “Throwing on third-and-3 was an incredible statement. Throwing at the goal line? That’s insane. ‘No, we’re throwing it,’ and it was awesome. I can’t tell you how awesome it was to be doing something no one else was doing in a unique way — and the frustration that you could put defenses in.” If becoming an innovator was easy to do, there would be more people doing it. item.title: Bobby Witt Jr. named finalist for AL MVP award
item.description: BOSTON, MA - SEPTEMBER 12: Bobby Witt Jr. #7 of the Kansas City Royals during the game against the Boston Red Sox at Fenway Park on September 12, 2026 in Boston, Massachusetts. (Photo By Winslow Townson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Now that the World Series is over, baseball can start handing out hardware. On Monday, shortstop Bobby Witt Jr. was named a finalist for AL Most Valuable Player for the second time in his career. Witt led the American League with 7.0 fWAR, and hit .281/.359/.441 with 18 home runs. He finished ninth in the league in hits (157), ninth in runs scored (94), sixth in doubles (33), second in steals (45), and ninth in Runs Created (95). He led all AL defenders with +24 Outs Above Average and was a finalist for a Gold Glove Award. Witt will be up against Astros outfielder Yordan Alvarez and Rays third baseman Junior Caminero. Witt finished second to Aaron Judge in 2024. He finished fourth in MVP voting last year, and seventh in 2023.George Brett is the only Royals player to win AL MVP, taking home the award in 1980. Carter Jensen was not named a finalist for AL Rookie of the Year, despite a strong season behind the plate. The Kansas City native hit .239/.323/.467 with 27 home runs and 65 walks, but was shutout in favor of Kevin McGonigle of the Tigers, Parker Messick of the Guardians, and Payton Tolle of the Red Sox. The MVP Awards will be announced on November 12, at 6 p.m. CT on MLB Network. item.title: USC wins season opener big, in return of JuJu Watkins
item.description: USC guard JuJu Watkins (12) drives towards the basket while guarded by UNLV forward Norah Moo (14) during second half of college basketball game against UNLV on Monday November 2, 2026 at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas. With 5:50 left in the first quarter of No. 3 USC’s season opener, JuJu Watkins made her first basket since March of 2025. The Trojans’ megastar made her return to the court in the team’s 100-68 win over UNLV at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas. “I think she physically looks great,” said USC Head Coach Lindsay Gottlieb. “It's just finding that rhythm.” There was so much anticipation for this day, not just at USC, but in the women’s basketball world at large. Despite justifiably looking unlike herself in the first half, the rust seemed to shake off by the end of the 3rd quarter. It included a dazzling reverse layup fans are accustomed to seeing. She finished with 21 points and 5 rebounds in 25 minutes of work. The casual observer would not have known Watkins hadn’t seen true competitive action in 19 months due to an ACL injury. “I mean obviously we're still we're still putting a restriction on on Juju's minutes just in the wrap up,” Gottlieb explained. “She's only gonna continue to get better, and she hasn't played in a competitive environment like this (since her injury).” Entering the game, Watkins was the major storyline. Once the ball tipped off, it was obvious she does not and will not have to do it all herself this season. Reigning Big 10 Rookie Of The Year, Jazzy Davidson had 23 points, 5 boards and 4 assists. America’s number one recruit, Saniyah Hall, finished with 22 points and 7 rebounds in her Trojan debut. “We have a lot of players that can do great things with the ball in their hands,” said Davidson. “But also we have a whole lot of unselfish players as well. And I think everybody's willing to make that extra pass to get the best shot.” While the arena wasn’t filled for a game in the middle of the afternoon on a Monday, there were plenty of Juju’s biggest supporters on hand. They came not only from the campus of USC, Los Angeles and Las Vegas, but from all over the country. “I love her,” said Velen Castillo, who came all the way from El Paso, Texas. “I've been following her since she was a freshman. She got hurt, she sat out. But she's back. And here I am.” Though, perhaps the most ardent fans in the house were the little girls who came to watch the return of their hero. There were youngsters in the crowd donning their buns atop their heads just like Watkins. “She's a good inspiration for kids, and I've been learn a lot from her and offer skills she has,” 12 year old Chelsea Lynn said. The impact off the court is evident. Watkins is a generational talent. On the court, Monday afternoon’s win was just one game in a marathon. A race USC hopes ends in early April.
